clusters.notes: (1) Maintainer review point, not a test failure: tools/AGENTS.md documents a host teardown invariant, 'Background-process teardown signals the parent first ... Never SIGTERM descendants before the parent' (Chromium zygotes reaped mid-shutdown turn exit 0 into a SIGTRAP core dump). #125004 sends one SIGTERM to the whole sandbox group, so the command and its descendants are signalled together. Main's sandbox branch never followed the host ordering (it only signals the wrapper, which is not the command), and the invariant is written against _terminate_host_pid, but a reviewer may ask whether it should extend to sandboxes. Making it parent-first needs the command's PID (the wrapper would have to background it and forward TERM), which is a redesign of #125004, not a fold-in; neither the regression test nor the probe can observe the difference without a zygote-style program. (2) Job control: every backend's execute() runs `bash -c`/`bash -lc` (base.py, ssh.py, singularity.py, modal.py, vercel_sandbox.py), and bash 5.3 honours `set -m` with no tty (jobcontrol-probe.log: wrapper PGID == PID; the group kill empties it). Simulated missing job control (NC-B, `set -m` removed): the group kill hits ESRCH and the command, its tree and the wrapper all keep running with a 'killed' receipt; main also leaves the command running (it kills only the wrapper), so this is not worse for the user command. Residual: a bash built without job control. Real docker/ssh/modal backends NOT_TESTED (no sandbox available); LocalEnvironment uses the same spawn-per-call bash -c model. (3) Fold-in cost: on a container whose PID 1 does not reap (docker_snap_compat without --init) the exited wrapper stays a zombie, `kill -0 -- -<pgid>` keeps succeeding, and the kill waits the full grace (2 s) before a no-op SIGKILL. Not tested. (4) Side effect of #125004 worth knowing: main's wrapper keeps the exec stdout pipe open, so a LocalEnvironment launch of a long command waits on the orphaned-pipe guard (about 0.46 s measured) and a pipe-capturing env without that guard (subprocess.run(capture_output=True)) hangs until its 10 s timeout and records failed_start; #125004's `> /dev/null 2>&1` on the wrapper removes that (0.02 s). clusters.notes: (1) Need confirmed on main 298a01c7: cron/executions.py:136-137 still `if started_at is None: return pid == os.getpid()` (unchanged since abc22cdf1a); #117584 fixed only the unreadable-current branch. cron/delivery_queue.py:24 imports the shared helper, so one line covers both ledgers, as #108484 states. (2) When is started_at NULL in production? create_execution, adopt_claimed_execution and delivery claim_next record `get_process_start_time(os.getpid())`, which returns None only when /proc/<pid>/stat is unreadable AND psutil fails (procfs absent or restricted in a sandbox/container; psutil itself reads /proc on Linux). Both columns exist in CREATE TABLE since they were introduced (abc22cdf1a, 3373e97693), so migrated legacy rows are not a source. The trigger is narrow, but the result is terminal (unknown is immutable), and the reporter reproduced it on native Windows with fault injection. (3) Residual risk the maintainer should know: with the fix, a NULL-fingerprint execution whose PID is later recycled is still bounded by the stale-claim sweep (_live_owner_stale_after_seconds), but delivery_queue.recover_abandoned has no wedge bound, so such a delivery stays 'delivering' while the recycled PID lives. That is the same trade-off main already accepted for the unreadable-current branch in #117584; kvnloo fork #60's at-most-once delivery split addresses it but contradicts #117584 and fails the contract, so it is not folded. (4) Rebase notes for #108484: drop its second hunk (on main already) and move its test sentinel past START_TIME_DRIFT_TOLERANCE (108484-own-test-rebase-fix.diff). (5) Fork-side: close kvnloo/hermes-agent#60 after #108484 merges.
